clue.text: Destroy poster etc, which must be suppressed

indicators.note: destroying the words breaks them up so their letters can be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to get rid of a poster and similar material that ought to be censored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroy' is the anagram signal on POSTER ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified material at the highest level of secrecy is exactly what must be kept hidden from view.

clue.text: Pa gets bottle cracked — it's for VIPs

indicators.note: a cracked bottle is broken, so the letters of the words are shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Father opens a bottle at a dinner meant for important guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' is the anagram signal on PA BOTTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: At a formal banquet the head table is where the most important guests are seated.

clue.text: Dead poppy head comes up as part of a flower

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dying poppy's flower head rises, revealing part of its bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns LATE plus P, giving PETAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured leaf-like segment of a blossom's corolla is a basic part of a flower.

clue.text: Philosophy of rationing? That will do!

definitions.meaning: playfully, the creed of one who rations is to stop when there is sufficient
an exclamation telling someone to stop, as patience has run out

explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase both calls a halt and, read literally, states that a sufficient amount is all one needs.

clue.text: Eliminate source abroad

parts.note: a root is an origin or source
being out can mean being away or abroad

explanation.surface: A command to get rid of supplies coming from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up completely, as a weed is pulled, is to eradicate or get rid of something.

clue.text: Counts everyone seen in neckwear

indicators.note: everyone is pictured inside the neckwear, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ties are worn round the neck
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Aristocrats, all of them seen wearing cravats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallies as a verb are records or reckonings of a total, so it matches counts as a verb.

clue.text: Crawl, perhaps, inside nuns' wimples

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the run of the phrase across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone creeping about within the headgear of nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' signals the run of letters across nunS WIMples.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is a stroke used in the water, so it is one example of this activity.

clue.text: New rafter constructed in plant

indicators.note: something constructed is assembled from parts, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A fresh roof beam has been built into a plant, as though in a greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed' is the anagram signal on NEW RAFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of small aquatic fern, so it is a type of plant.

clue.text: Ill-tempered doctor got up from bed

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a military doctor
one who rose got up after sleep

explanation.surface: A grumpy physician dragging himself out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullen and gloomy in mood describes someone ill-humoured or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Make printer do graph, which is above criticism

indicators.note: an instruction to make something of the words, rebuilding their letters into a new phrase

explanation.surface: An instruction to get a printer to produce a chart that nobody could fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is the anagram signal on PRINTER DO GRAPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entirely fitting and correct cannot reasonably be faulted, so the idiom means beyond reproach.

clue.text: Terrace where a senior citizen keeps that thing turning

indicators.note: turning the whole construction round means it is read backwards
the senior citizen holds the other piece within

parts.note: OAP, old-age pensioner, is a British term for a retired person
it refers to that thing

explanation.surface: An outdoor paved space where a pensioner keeps something spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' and 'turning' together build the whole word backwards: the pensioner holding the pronoun, then read in reverse. OAP means old-age pensioner in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved area beside a house is a terrace, the usual British sense.

clue.text: Being a cleaner, lift or lie around

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner hefting things or lazing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cleaner' looks like a person who cleans houses; it is an engine part.
explanation.definitionFit: This engine component removes impurities from lubricant, so it is a device that cleans.

clue.text: One left leg half rose in a lively manner

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A dancer with one leg raised halfway, moving briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical tempo direction from Italian tells players to perform at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: Resides with Spanish girl, accommodating her

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room, so the girl's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Ines is a Spanish girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lives with a young Spanish woman who puts her up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be inherent in something is to exist or dwell within it, a formal sense of residing.

clue.text: Make more efficient as I lock the pin for a change

indicators.note: the words are changed around so their letters form a new phrase

explanation.surface: A suggestion to improve things by securing the pin oneself, just this once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' is the anagram signal on AS I LOCK THE PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something into proper working order is to knock it into shape, improving its effectiveness.

clue.text: Big editor absorbed in comic, which is to fold

indicators.note: the pieces are soaked up inside the comic, so they go within it

parts.note: a clown is a comic
OS, outsize, is a clothing label for large sizes

explanation.surface: A large-framed editor engrossed in a comic book that is about to cease publication.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label, a crossword favourite for 'big'.
explanation.definitionFit: When a business folds it ceases trading, which is what shutting it permanently means.

clue.text: Idolaters he meets somewhere in Greece

parts.note: taken as written
Athens is the Greek capital

explanation.surface: A man visiting a Greek city where false gods were once worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagans who worship idols rather than the god of the main faiths are called by this old term.

clue.text: More than a hairdo and a knees-up would be an excess

parts.note: over means more than
a bun is hair coiled at the back of the head
a knees-up is British slang for a lively party with dancing, so a dance

explanation.surface: A fancy hairstyle plus a party would be overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is a British word for a boisterous party.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus beyond what is needed is an excess, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Draught wine could be terminal

parts.note: a draught is a current of air
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Wine served on tap might prove fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is a building where flights depart, part of a place for planes.

clue.text: In difficulties, but not grounded?

definitions.meaning: literally perched up among branches, off the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a fix, and literally describes being up off the ground in branches.

clue.text: Shut up for a second, that is to say

parts.note: to wit means namely, that is to say

explanation.surface: A request to stay quiet for a moment, namely.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang order means be quiet, telling someone to stop talking.

clue.text: They have little money for drunken toper? Oh!

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drinker exclaims over the cash spent on drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' is the anagram signal on TOPER OH.
explanation.definitionFit: People lacking wealth are collectively described with this plural noun phrase.

clue.text: Informed sailor takes river, which leads to the Orient

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable seaman sails a river toward Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up to date with news is to be kept informed of it.

clue.text: Expert artist seen climbing palm tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: an ace is an expert
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A skilled painter spotted scaling a palm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ACERA upward to give ARECA. RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genus of tropical palm, source of the betel nut.

clue.text: Wicked dog owner gains right to be a lawbreaker

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in another piece
wicked suggests twisted or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An evil dog-owner gets the law on his side despite breaking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' rearranges DOG OWNER into WONGDOER; 'gains' puts R after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: One who commits a crime or wrong is an offender against the law.

clue.text: Scrap that sounds like a truce

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is said the same way as a word for truce

parts.note: a truce brings peace

explanation.surface: A fight that resembles a ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap of something is a small part or bit of it.

clue.text: Attitude? It's time to acquire one

explanation.surface: Perhaps it is time someone developed a better outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: The manner or mood conveyed, as in a tone of voice, expresses one's stance.

clue.text: The British duck notices area of fresh water

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O
ads are advertisements or notices

explanation.surface: A British duck reading signs on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BROADS are a network of rivers and lakes in Norfolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This English waterway region of shallow lakes is a well-known freshwater area.
